patches.updated_disclaimer: Statewide averages derived from NOAA reporting stations. Desert Southwest and Gulf Coast dominate; Alaska and Hawaii have essentially zero. Includes Washington DC.
Statewide averages from NOAA station normals. Elevation and latitude drive rankings — some interior western states outrank their eastern peers of similar latitude. Includes Washington DC.
Flash density = cloud-to-ground lightning strikes per square mile per year, averaged across the state. Vaisala NLDN is the standard reference dataset used by NOAA/NWS. Includes Washington DC.
A 'severe thunderstorm day' is any calendar day with at least one qualifying severe report in the state (hail >= 1 in, wind >= 58 mph, or tornado). Definition per NOAA SPC. Includes Washington DC.
Counts only cities that are legally incorporated municipalities; CDPs (census-designated places) and unincorporated communities are excluded. Includes Washington DC.
Uses incorporated city (not metro area) population. Includes Washington DC.
Uses each state's largest incorporated city (not metro area). Includes Washington DC.
Ranks each state by the population of its designated capital city, not its largest city. Includes Washington DC.
Uses the Census Bureau's 2020 definition of urban areas (≥5,000 people or ≥2,000 housing units in a contiguous developed area). Includes Washington DC.
Rank 1 = the MOST rural state. Uses the Census 2020 urban-area definition. Includes Washington DC.
Uses architectural height (top of spire/roof) per CTBUH, not antenna height. Only completed buildings — under-construction towers excluded. Includes Washington DC.
Counts total F500 HQs in the state, not the number of distinct cities that host one. Includes Washington DC.
Counts all active Amtrak-served stations, including thruway bus-only connections at some stops. Includes Washington DC.
Uses the Census-defined MSA (not CSA / combined). MSAs that cross state lines are credited to the state containing the principal city. Includes Washington DC.
Only incorporated cities are counted; CDPs excluded. Ties broken alphabetically for consecutive ranks. Includes Washington DC.
Counts Title IV degree-granting institutions in a single principal city (not the whole metro). Boston's total is inflated by many small specialty and religious institutions. Includes Washington DC.

Uses NOAA's 'general coastline' figures (straight-line, excludes bays and river tidal reaches). Great Lakes shorelines excluded — this ranks ocean/tidal coastline only. DC not included (source omits it).

Includes states with a shared land or river border with Canada, ordered by length of shared border in miles. States whose only Canadian boundary is a Great Lake shoreline are excluded. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Only 4 states share a land border with Mexico. Ordered by length of shared border. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
'Landlocked' here means no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shoreline. States along the Mississippi or other inland rivers still qualify. Includes Washington DC.
